title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay, Including Salary Sacrifice Travel Expenses
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual pay using the 38-hour week formula. Includes tax, super, and how salary sacrifice travel expenses can affect your take-home pay.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours (38 × 52).

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. Remember that this calculation assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is the current National Minimum Wage in Australia?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and apply to employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates may be higher for specific industries or roles.

faqs.q: How does salary sacrifice travel expenses affect my tax?
faqs.a: Salary sacrifice travel expenses allow you to use pre-tax income to pay for work-related travel, reducing your taxable income. For example, if you salary sacrifice $5,000 for travel, your taxable income drops by that amount, potentially lowering your tax bracket. However, this arrangement must be through your employer and comply with Australian Taxation Office rules. Our estimate does not include salary packaging, so your actual tax may differ.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you're paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, understanding your annual equivalent is essential for budgeting, comparing jobs, and planning tax. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This article assumes a full-time working week of 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. If you work part-time or different hours, simply replace 38 with your usual weekly hours. The result is your gross annual income before tax, Medicare levy, and superannuation.

### Why 52 Weeks?

A year has 52 weeks. Multiplying your weekly pay by 52 gives a straightforward annual figure. Some calculations use 52.18 to account for leap years, but 52 is standard for most pay periods and is used by the Australian Bureau of Statistics for average earnings.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a 38-hour week at the National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour), weekly pay is $1,004.90, so fortnightly is $2,009.80. This can help you match your pay cycle.

## Key Pay Concepts

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for full-time and part-time employees. However, most workers are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that may specify higher rates. Always check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website. Our [pay guides](/blog) can help you find the right rate.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. For the minimum wage, that's $33.05 per hour. When using our [the timesheet](/), you can check a box to add casual loading. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it automatically.

### Superannuation Guarantee

Your employer must pay superannuation on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual gross pay is $60,000, your employer contributes an additional $7,200 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it's paid separately. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross pay is the starting point for tax calculations. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The reduction thresholds for singles (2025–26) are used here as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. If your income is below a certain level, the levy may be reduced or waived.

### How Salary Sacrifice Travel Expenses Can Help

One way to reduce your taxable income is through salary sacrifice arrangements. If your employer offers it, you can use pre-tax dollars to pay for work-related travel expenses, such as flights, accommodation, or vehicle costs. This lowers your assessable income, potentially moving you to a lower tax bracket or reducing your Medicare levy. For example, if you earn $80,000 and salary sacrifice $5,000 in travel expenses, your taxable income becomes $75,000. You pay less tax and Medicare levy, but your super guarantee may also be affected because it's based on your reduced ordinary earnings. Always consult the Australian Taxation Office or a tax professional before entering a salary sacrifice agreement.

## Average Earnings Comparison

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees in May 2026 were $2,083.70. That's an annual equivalent of about $108,352 (using 52 weeks). For all employees (including part-time), total average weekly earnings were $1,579.20, or about $82,118 annually. These are averages, not medians for a specific job. Our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page has more detail.

## Using the Timesheet

Our [the timesheet](/) is designed to help you convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Enter your base hourly rate, select whether you're casual (to add 25% loading), and the tool calculates gross pay. It also estimates tax and Medicare levy using the 2026–27 rates, and shows super at 12% on top. Remember that this is an estimate – it does not include penalty rates, allowances, unpaid overtime, or salary packaging. For a more precise calculation, refer to your pay slip or speak with your employer.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
